header: This is the data of the DSP story card (pure, no React): how the Durgapur Steel Plant came to be, who made it, what it made at the start, who has headed it, and the family of SAIL it belongs to. Every fact carries its SOURCE. I rank the sources in this order of weight:
* SAIL's own publications: "Steel Cities" (2020), the Background & History page and its History Tree of dated photographs, the plant's page and its RTI manual, the annual reports.
* The Ministry of Steel (a 2002 backgrounder; the 2025-26 annual report; a Lok Sabha reply), the Government's and SAIL's own records.
* The plant's and SAIL's JO Manuals 2022 (the five manuals read for this card; the page is given).

* A MEMOIR by M S Srinivasan, who served Hindustan Steel and SAIL for over thirty years and was part of the team that built Durgapur ("Durgapur - fifty years ago", 2010). It is the only source for the early heads' order and for some colour. It is a personal account, so wherever I use it the card says so, and where SAIL's captions confirm a name or a date the card says that too. I do not repeat its remarks on persons.

A date is the date the source gives; where two sources differ I show BOTH (the card says "the sources differ"). A name or year that no source gives I leave out: the card has gaps and says so, it never fills one. The pictures are SAIL's own photographs (SAIL's History Tree and its Steel Cities book), kept in public/dsp-history/ with the SAIL caption; their credit is on the card. Tested in history.selftest.ts.

symbols.name: Source
doc: A source, as the card shows it, so that the reader can CHECK it against the document: name the document; url where it is (none for the plant's internal JO manuals, which are named by file); pages the PRINTED page numbers cited (what the reader sees at the foot of the page); `page` is the same as text ("p. 67", "pp. 65, 87"); spread the document prints two pages on each page of the PDF (SAIL's Steel Cities does), so printed p. 87 is PDF page 44 and the link must say #page=44, not #page=87; offset the PDF page is the printed page plus this (the annual reports have two or six covers and contents pages before page 1), so printed p. 54 of SAIL's 2024-25 report is PDF page 56; quote the words of the document that carry the claim, verbatim, so the reader can match them with the text on the page; find for a web page (no page numbers): the sentence to highlight when the link is opened (a "text fragment", which Chrome, Edge and Safari follow; other browsers open the page and the quote is there to search for).

behaviours: nineteen pictures, each a real JPEG file in public/dsp-history of a sensible size
every file in the folder is used by a picture (no stray files), and the source of a picture is a path under /dsp-history/
every picture has a caption and a credit that says whose photograph it is: SAIL's, or (for the six portraits supplied for the card) that it was supplied and its source is not recorded

the dates of the pictures are SAIL's own (checked against its History Tree and Steel Cities): coke ovens November 23, 1959, blast furnace December 26, 1959, Queen February 1961, Section Mill February 18, 1961, Merchant Mill January 19, 1962, Wheel Plant January 24, 1962, Shastri January 11, 1964, Indira Gandhi 1970, modernisation January 23, 1985
21 entries with distinct ids, in date order, each with at least one source
an entry dated to the day agrees with its sort key (February 18, 1961 -> 1961-02-18)
an entry with a picture dated to the day carries the picture's date (Section Mill, Merchant Mill, Wheel Plant, blast furnace, coke ovens, Shastri, modernisation)
every date is written the American way, month first (December 26, 1959): no day-first date and no abbreviated month anywhere in the card's data
a full date in a sentence is followed by a comma after the year ("December 26, 1959, as"), as in the Chicago and AP rule
ISCON is spelled out where it first appears (the key dates and the facts): Indian Steel Works Construction Company

"SAIL Day" is NOT claimed: no source read for the card says January 24 is celebrated as SAIL Day (the History page, the manuals and the annual reports do not), so the card says only that SAIL was incorporated on January 24, 1973
initials of the heads are written without full stops (P C Niyogi, K K Sen), one spelling of each name
the memoir prints "K Sen", not "K K Sen": the card says so where it names the memoir's spelling, and never says the memoir writes K K Sen
the Queen at the Durgapur Club is credited to Steel Cities (2020), p. 66 (PDF page 34 of the book, where its caption is), and the visit's sources link to that page

every credit line leads to the EXACT place of its picture: eleven pictures the book prints link to the PDF page that carries them (printed page -> PDF page, two to a sheet; the Coates picture p. 86, President p. 87, Shastri p. 86, Indira Gandhi p. 87, Merchant Mill p. 88, Sathe p. 88, coke ovens p. 89, panorama p. 4, Section Mill and Niyogi p. 8, Club p. 66), opened on the whole page (view=Fit) so there is nothing to scroll; the one picture the book does not print (Nehru at the Wheel Plant) and Mr Mishra's portrait link to their web page at their own words; the six supplied portraits (source not recorded) have no link
every entry's picture exists, and so does every further picture of an entry (the Queen's visit carries two: with Mr Niyogi and at the Durgapur Club)

where the sources differ the entry says so: the Coates mission (1955 against 1956), the first blast furnace (26 against December 29, 1959; Kasturba against Sharada Devi), the Merchant Mill (1961 against January 19, 1962), Shastri's title in 1964
the five key dates and the facts are present: contract October 1956, construction January 1957, blast furnace December 26, 1959, first ingot April 24, 1960 (DSP Day), SAIL January 24, 1973
the facts that were checked: British technology (Rourkela German, Bhilai Soviet), 6,568 hectares, Rs 189.6 crore with Rs 17.36 crore for the township, 158 km from Kolkata

the plant's early steps are in the timeline: Coates 1955, ISCON contract October 1956, construction January 1957, coke ovens November 1959, first ingot April 24, 1960, Queen February 1961, 1.6 MT stage August 6, 1969, SAIL January 24, 1973
the Queen's visit is dated to the month SAIL gives (February 1961); no exact day is stated anywhere in the card, because no source read for it gives one
Pandit Nehru's two visits are as SAIL dates them: Section Mill February 18, 1961 and Wheel Plant January 24, 1962; Dr B C Roy's Merchant Mill January 19, 1962
seven parts of 'Who made it', each with a lead, points and sources; the Queen, Nehru, Dr Roy, Britain and the President are among them
'Rani Kuthi' and Suite No. 1: the Queen's night at Durgapur House is in the card
the Niyogi of the site (Jnananjan) and the General Manager (P C) are kept apart, not merged

five first items, in the order the units opened (iron, steel in ingots, the Section Mill, the Merchant Mill, the Wheel and Axle Plant), each with sources; NO item is called bars or rounds, and the Merchant Mill's item says that what it first rolled is not stated

the Merchant Mill's item ties plain rounds and TMT bars to the 1992 modernisation as the plant manual does (p. 37), never to the start; it shows the 1961 / January 1962 difference and the 'sources differ' note
the Section Mill's item shows February 18, 1961 (SAIL's photograph) against March 1961 (the Ministry), and the 'sources differ' note

the memoir's list of early products (billets, blooms, bars, commercial sections) is NOT among the items: it is shown apart, in its own words, marked a recollection, with the caution that no SAIL document lists the early products
what is unknown is said once: DSP's own tonnes for 1959-62 are not in any source; the only early figure is all of Hindustan Steel's, 0.158 MT in 1959-60 and 1.6 MT in 1961-62
the heads (as many as are listed) have distinct ids, are in date order, each with a basis and a source
five eras in order: General Manager, Director-in-Charge, Managing Director, Chief Executive Officer, Director In-charge; every head belongs to one and the eras follow the heads' order
the four heads that SAIL's own captions name (K Sen, P C Niyogi, D J Bell, B P Wadhera) are 'SAIL record' and have a SAIL picture

Dr Subir Kumar Bhattacharyya: full name, Managing Director from 2001 to December 2005, resting on the INAE obituary (an "Obituary" basis, a PDF source cited on page 1 with the words of the obituary), no picture

Shyam Bahadur Singh: full name (the press report of 1997 prints S B Singh), 1993 to 2001 from the profile in Skipper Limited's annual report 2014-15 (a "Company report", PDF page offset 2, cited on printed page 34 with the profile's own words), the 1997 press report kept as a second source, and the missing-MD notice ends at him

every head's chip (SAIL record, Memoir, Obituary, Company report, Press report, SAIL report, Annual report) opens a source of the kind it names, at its place: a cited PDF page where there is one (opened on that PDF page, shown whole), else the web page at its sentence

the chips open the right documents: K K Sen, Niyogi, Bell and Wadhera (SAIL record) the Steel Cities pages that print their pictures (PDF pages 45, 5, 44, 44) not the History Tree slideshow; the memoir's four its blog page at the sentence; Bhattacharyya the INAE obituary page 1; S B Singh the Skipper annual report (PDF page 36); B P Singh the 2022-23 annual report (PDF page 55)

the numbering is never done by hand: a head written anywhere in the list, even last, takes its place by date, and every head after it is numbered one higher by itself; taking one out closes the gap; the gap notes follow the ids
the four known only from the memoir (R K Chatterjee, A N Banerjee, Bhagaram Tulpule, P K Paul) are marked 'Memoir' and have no picture

the dated heads are as the documents give them: MD Bajaj from November 1, 2009 (after V Shyamsundar, to October 31, 2009), CEO P K Singh May 2012 to December 2015, A K Rath from March 2016, DIC B P Singh from April 19, 2022, Surajit Mishra from July 15, 2025
the interim of 2025 is shown as held in turn (Anirban Dasgupta, Alok Verma), not as a head's term
the gaps are stated in words and attach to a head that exists: 1970s-1993, 2005-2009, 2009-2012, after Rath, 2019-2022
pictures of heads exist; the others show initials (K K Sen -> KS, P C Niyogi -> PN, Major General B P Wadhera -> BW, Anirban Dasgupta and Alok Verma -> AD)
SAIL's foundation: Hindustan Steel January 19, 1954 and SAIL January 24, 1973 (Rs 2,000 crore) are there, with the 1978 restructuring and the later mergers
nine units with their sources; Durgapur is the one marked as this plant; Britain, Germany and the USSR are the partners of DSP, RSP and BSP/BSL

each unit has its short form as SAIL prints it (BSP, RSP, DSP, BSL, ISP, ASP, SSP, VISL, CFP), and the manual's own words for the full name with the short form in brackets are quoted among its sources, on the page given
the names of the units carry no town or short form of their own (the card adds the short form to the right of the name and the town beside the state)

every one of SAIL's other bodies says WHERE it is (town and state, or the states for the mines): the Central Marketing Organisation in Kolkata, West Bengal (headquarters), the Refractory Unit at Bokaro, the R&D Centre, the Management Training Institute, the Centre for Engineering & Technology and the Safety Organisation at Ranchi, the Coal Supply Organisation at Dhanbad (all Jharkhand), SAILCON in New Delhi, the mines in Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh
each place is in a source's own words: SAIL's annual report 2025-26 (printed pp. 206-207) or its page for the body, or the manual (the Coal Supply Organisation at Dhanbad, the mines)
the other bodies' short forms are SAIL's own: CMO, MTI, CET, RDCIS, SSO, SRU, SAILCON, CCSO; each is in the quoted words of its source

the Visvesvaraya plant is VISL first and VISP also, as SAIL's own plant page and the plant's website write it; the sources quote SAIL's plant page, the plant's website, and the JO manual's heading with VISP and its text with VISL

its history is short and SAIL's own, with the difference shown: founded 1918 (SAIL's plant page) against 1923 (the plant's website); renamed VISL in 1976; a SAIL subsidiary from August 18, 1989; no 1998 merger is claimed, because no SAIL or Ministry document read says so; the lines are short

the position of the three units under disinvestment is stated with its sources: Visvesvaraya (closure directed in October 2022, 245 employees in July 2024, withdrawal asked on January 30, 2026), Alloy Steels Plant (two attempts, withdrawal asked) and Salem (bids annulled); the others have no such line
DSP's capacity on the card is SAIL's own page: hot metal 2.45, crude steel 2.20, saleable steel 2.12 MT
other bodies are listed with a page of a SAIL document and the words of every source
million tonnes are MT: no 'lakh' and no 'Mt' anywhere in the card's data
no Bengali letters and no question-mark placeholders
the memoir is named for what it is wherever it is used, and its remarks on persons are not repeated (no hearsay words)
the card never claims who is not on a source: no head is given a tenure that no source dates (Chatterjee, Banerjee, Tulpule, Paul carry 'no date given' or a rough period)
the Steel Authority of India Limited is named in full with SAIL in parentheses after it, in the timeline and in SAIL's story
there are over two hundred cited uses of a source in the card, found by walking its data
every cited page is also written as text in the same words (pages [67] -> "p. 67", [65, 87] -> "pp. 65, 87"), so the text and the link can never disagree
every source cited at a page, or at a sentence, shows the words of the source (a quote), which the reader can match with the page

a source with a web address links to the PAGE cited, not to the top of the document: Steel Cities printed p. 87 is PDF page 44 (two printed pages to a PDF page), p. 8 is PDF page 5, p. 65 is 33, p. 67 is 34, p. 89 is 45, p. 6 is 4

the annual reports' printed pages are moved to the PDF's own: SAIL 2024-25 p. 54 is PDF page 56, SAIL 2022-23 p. 165 is PDF 167, SAIL 2025-26 p. 49 is PDF 51, the Ministry's 2025-26 report p. 35 is PDF 41; the Lok Sabha reply p. 2 is PDF 2
the plant's two JO manuals (internal files, no web address) are named with their file number and cited by the page printed, which is also the page of the PDF; they have no link and say so
a web page (no page numbers) is cited at a SENTENCE of it: the link carries a text fragment that highlights it; every web use that quotes has the same sentence to look for
the text fragment is written safely: a hyphen, comma and ampersand in the sentence are percent-escaped, so the browser finds it
no use of a source cites a page that Steel Cities, which has 70 PDF pages (140 printed), cannot have, and none cites the chapter's title page (p. 63), which carries no text
the Lok Sabha reply is named with the date it was answered, April 5, 2023 (not the year of the file's folder)
